hints: Focus on what two separate regions you must see at the same time, one for the carbonyl and one for the hydroxyl.
Look first for a strong sharp dip for $C=O$ around 1670 to 1750 $cm^{-1}$, then check the high wavenumber end for $O-H$.
Remember a carboxylic acid $O-H$ is very broad and sits at 2500 to 3000 $cm^{-1}$, while an alcohol $O-H$ is broad at 3200 to 3650 $cm^{-1}$, so match both peaks together.
walkthrough:
**List the target absorptions**

You need two things in the same spectrum. A strong $C=O$ stretch and an $O-H$ stretch.

From the table:
$$C=O \text{ at } 1640-1750 \text{ } cm^{-1} \text{ (sharp, strong) }$$
$$O-H \text{ (carboxyl) at } 2500-3000 \text{ } cm^{-1} \text{ (very broad) }$$
$$O-H \text{ (hydroxy) at } 3200-3650 \text{ } cm^{-1} \text{ (broad) }$$

**Check for the C=O peak**

Look near 1700 $cm^{-1}$ for a deep dip down to low transmittance. This is the fingerprint for a carbonyl group.

Spectra A, B and D all have a strong peak here, but spectrum C has no strong peak in this region, so C cannot contain $C=O$.

**Check the O-H region and decide**

Now look at 2500 to 3650 $cm^{-1}$. Remember transmittance dips down means absorption.

Only spectrum B shows both a strong $C=O$ dip near 1700 $cm^{-1}$ AND a very broad, deep absorption covering about 2500 to 3300 $cm^{-1}$. That broad shape is classic for a carboxylic acid $O-H$, which contains both $C=O$ and $O-H$ together.

options.A: Has a strong $C=O$ peak near 1700 $cm^{-1}$ but lacks a broad $O-H$ absorption. The small sharp peak near 3400 $cm^{-1}$ is too narrow and weak for $O-H$, it fits $N-H$ of an amide or amine. This is the amide trap.
options.B: Shows exactly what is needed. Strong sharp $C=O$ absorption around 1700 $cm^{-1}$ plus a very broad $O-H$ absorption from about 2500 to 3300 $cm^{-1}$. This combination is characteristic of a carboxylic acid, $RCOOH$, which contains both $C=O$ and $O-H$.
options.C: Shows sharp $C-H$ peaks near 2850 to 3100 $cm^{-1}$ and a $C=C$ peak near 1450 $cm^{-1}$, but no strong $C=O$ peak near 1700 $cm^{-1}$ and no broad $O-H$ band. Likely a hydrocarbon or alkene.
options.D: Shows a broad $O-H$ band for an alcohol around 3200 to 3600 $cm^{-1}$, so it does contain $O-H$. However it has no strong $C=O$ peak near 1700 $cm^{-1}$, so it cannot contain $C=O$. This is the alcohol-only trap.
